reason: issue #238 rest back to a note: the editor could turn a note into a rest and had no inverse. The six tests: arrow keys reach a rest and step off it again, including back across a barline onto a rest in the previous measure (a rest cannot be clicked - the renderer's positional map indexes sounding notes only - so the arrow walk is the only way in); a digit on a selected rest makes a note that keeps the rest's duration, type, dots and voice, with the bar still summing to the same per-voice total and the whole-model audit clean; the new note's pitch is the one the instrument's tuning gives for the string chosen on the panel at that fret (Rule 5's string/staff-tuning-line mirror), not the fret alone; the converted note deletes back to a rest, restoring the same counts and the same bar shape, with the render agreeing at both ends and the rest still arrow-reachable afterwards; the converted document saves through the transcription PUT and, after a full page reload, is still a note on the same string and fret with every octave inside MusicXML's 0-9 range; and the rest address space is the document's rests in document order across measures and voices, with out-of-range indices null on both sides.
